title: unified-rollouts: add stability guards and observability for canary/AB/shadow autorollback workflow
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent rollouts where transient metric spikes (downstream latency and increased error noise) caused noisy autorollback decisions during staged canary + shadow traffic experiments. This PR adds stability guards and enhanced observability to the unified rollouts autorollback workflow so rollbacks are only triggered by sustained, quorum-backed signals and engineers can triage faster. Changes include: 1) Quorum-based metric aggregation: require N-out-of-M metric sources (region shards / routing proxies / canary probes) to exceed thresholds for T consecutive windows before a rollback is considered. 2) Time-window smoothing: add an exponential moving-window check and configurable stabilization window per rollout policy. 3) Quarantine stage: introduce an optional quarantine probe stage that isolates suspect traffic for realtime inspection without impacting the baseline. 4) Enhanced telemetry: emit detailed rollout decision traces, per-probe contributions, and candidate-model health snapshots to the rollout tracing view and a new rollback_decision metric series. 5) E2E tests and chaos scenarios: add integration tests that simulate transient spikes, region splits, and probe flapping to validate no false-positive rollbacks. 6) Backwards-compatible config: rollout policies default to the previous behavior unless the new flags (quorum_size, consecutive_windows, quarantine_enabled) are enabled. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-7890 - [x] unit tests for quorum evaluation - [x] integration/e2e tests for transient spike scenarios - [x] added metrics and traces - [x] canary + shadow rollout tested in staging - [x] docs updated for rollout config flags Runtime impact: small CPU overhead on the rollout controller from additional aggregation and state tracking; added metrics labeled to minimize cardinality. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature flag in staging for 48h, run automated e2e and production-like traffic replay, then enable by default for Dedicated customers, and finally roll out to hosted with a gradual ramp. Related: ENG-8012 (observe rollback_decision traces), SUP-4421 (customer case where a transient SLO spike caused an unnecessary rollback).
